recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Future messaging or MessageHeader changes should preserve the distinction that MessageHeader may be stored locally, but post-processing resource interpretation must not depend on looking up a previous MessageHeader.
issue_request: FHIR-41271 was an Applied/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-core messaging issue for R6 asking whether MessageHeader is transient and whether receivers should discard it after processing. The resolution was to add a messaging-page subsection clarifying that MessageHeader is necessary to understand a message bundle, but once resources are processed into another context, MessageHeader content SHALL NOT be required to interpret those resources.
initial_application: Commit 48603ec9f67f91177955f8470fed7caad80596e4 applied FHIR-41271 together with FHIR-40294, FHIR-42716, and FHIR-43942 by adding the requested MessageHeader and REST subsection and implementation note to source/messaging.html. The present source still contains the same rule, with only minor punctuation, link, and capitalization differences from the Jira prose.
additional_context: The linked FHIR-I Zulip thread confirms the normative point: systems SHALL NOT have to retain or consult MessageHeader after message processing to understand persisted resources. FHIR-I minutes record the 15-0-0 Persuasive with Modification vote, and InM minutes plus related Zulip discussion clarify that MessageHeader may still be persisted for audit, but persistent interpretive context belongs in resources such as Task, Provenance, Composition, or the payload itself.
reconciliation: No source edit was made. The current source/messaging.html section is in build scope and already conveys the approved clarification and implementation note; moving the subsection or matching Jira punctuation literally would be editorial churn without changing implementer understanding.
